title: First and second moment bound for low degree
statement: Let $n,k$ be natural numbers, and let $p$ be a coefficient family on the subsets of the $n$ coordinates, with $p(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>k$. If $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S$ is the Walsh character, then $\displaystyle e^{-2k}\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)^2\leq\left(\mathbb E_{x\sim\mathrm{Unif}(\{0,1\}^n)}|P(x)|\right)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: coefficient family $p$ on subsets of the $n$ coordinates
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients; degree at most $k$ means $a_S=0$ for $|S|>k$. If $P$ has degree at most the integer $k\ge0$, then $e^{-2k}\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S^2\le(\mathbb E|P|)^2$.
